commands.review_summary:
Adds a fixed 30-second deadline and caller-cancellation forwarding to Google Chat’s guarded Google authentication fetch transport, with focused regression tests.

PR surface: Source +9, Tests +159. Total +168 across 2 files.

Reproducibility: yes. at source level: current main has the unbounded guarded-fetch call, and pinned Gaxios forwards caller cancellation into this fetch seam. The PR has not supplied an unmocked current-head reproduction through the real guard.
commands.review_followup: - [P1] The remaining merge gates are contributor-supplied real behavior proof and routine exact-head test cleanup; ClawSweeper should not manufacture the contributor’s proof.

target.title: fix(googlechat): add timeout to Google auth fetch requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Google Chat auth requests made through `createGoogleAuthFetch()` — the shared fetch implementation injected into Gaxios as the Google auth transport — had no request deadline. Token refresh, cert fetch, and any other HTTP auth operation could wait indefinitely when a Google auth endpoint accepted the connection but never responded.

## Why This Change Was Made

- A 30s request timeout (`GOOGLE_AUTH_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`) is added to the `fetchWithSsrFGuard` call inside `createGoogleAuthFetch()`. This matches the deadline used by Vertex ADC (#102050), Chutes OAuth (#102026), MiniMax OAuth (#102862), Google Chat cert fetch (#102924), and every other control-plane auth path.
- Any caller-provided `AbortSignal` is extracted from the sanitized init and passed as the guard's `signal` parameter so `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` composes it with the 30s deadline.
- The existing SSRF policy, dispatcher routing, body-size limit, response buffering, and release lifecycle are unchanged.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: a hanging Google auth endpoint now aborts within the 30s deadline instead of waiting indefinitely.

Real environment tested: local Linux Node source checkout; real `node:http` loopback server that receives the auth request and deliberately never responds.

Exact command run after this patch: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/googlechat/src/google-auth.runtime.test.ts`

Evidence after fix: the focused regression creates a real loopback HTTP server, calls `createGoogleAuthFetch()` with the server's base URL, and asserts the hanging connection is aborted with an `AbortError`/`TimeoutError` within a bounded window. The test verifies the production `timeoutMs` is 30_000 and proves exactly one request reached the hanging server before the abort fired.

What was not tested: live Google OAuth endpoints; no live Google Cloud credentials were available. The hang is reproduced with a real local HTTP server, not the real third-party service.

### Regression tests added

| Test | What it proves |
|------|------|
| `passes a 30s timeout deadline to guarded Google auth fetches` | `timeoutMs` is 30_000 in the guard call |
| `times out a hanging Google auth request on a real stalled connection` | Real loopback server + real `globalThis.fetch` → connection hangs → aborts |
| `forwards a caller AbortSignal so the guard composes it with the deadline` | Caller signal is passed through to `fetchWithSsrFGuard.signal` |
| `rejects when the caller aborts before the 30s guard deadline` | External abort at <30s preempts the fixed deadline → `AbortError` |
